mechanism_narrative: Sustained improvement in WORKPLACES mobility (rising from -28.6% to -19.6% over four weeks) signals resumption of commuting and office occupancy. This restores weekday retail foot traffic and shopping patterns, driving RETAIL_REC higher over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved 9 percentage points over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not exceed the mean of the prior 28 days, or WORKPLACES reverses to decline in week t+1.

mechanism_narrative: Declining PARKS mobility (from -9.4% to -18.0%) indicates reduced outdoor leisure substitution. Consumers redirect discretionary time and spending back to indoor retail and recreation venues, increasing RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS declines more than 5 percentage points over two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS fell 8.6 percentage points from t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next four weeks, or PARKS mobility reverses upward by more than 3 percentage points in week t+1.

mechanism_narrative: Stable GROCERY_PHARM mobility (consistently 6.3–7.4%) combined with rising WORKPLACES indicates essential-goods demand is met and work routines are normalizing. Consumers shift discretionary spending to retail and recreation, driving RETAIL_REC upward over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises above -20% AND GROCERY_PHARM remains above 6%
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than or equal to the prior 28-day mean, or either WORKPLACES falls below -25% or GROCERY_PHARM drops below 5% in any week.

mechanism_narrative: Persistent TRANSIT depression (around -45% to -51%) signals ongoing mobility restrictions or low commuter confidence. If TRANSIT remains suppressed below -40% for two consecutive weeks, retail venues remain underutilized and RETAIL_REC stays depressed or declines further over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT remains below -40% for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT at -45.6% in t-0w, -46.4% in t-1w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days exceeds the prior 14-day mean by more than 2 percentage points, or TRANSIT rises above -35% in week t+1.

mechanism_narrative: Mid-November in Delhi marks the onset of favorable weather (post-monsoon, pre-winter peak). Rising PARKS mobility would signal seasonal leisure demand. However, observed PARKS decline suggests weather is not yet driving outdoor substitution; retail venues remain competitive, supporting stable or rising RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS does not rise above -10% within two weeks
failure_condition: PARKS mobility rises above -5% and RETAIL_REC declines over the next 28 days, or RETAIL_REC falls below -15%.

mechanism_narrative: Elevated RESIDENTIAL mobility (6.9–9.6%) combined with depressed TRANSIT indicates people remain home-based and avoid public transport. This suppresses retail foot traffic. RETAIL_REC will remain depressed or decline further over the next four weeks unless RESIDENTIAL mobility drops below 5%.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL remains above 6% AND TRANSIT remains below -40%
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days exceeds the prior 28-day mean, or RESIDENTIAL drops below 5% while TRANSIT rises above -35%.

mechanism_narrative: Week-on-week improvement in WORKPLACES (t-3w: -28.6% → t-0w: -19.6%) is a one-week leading indicator of retail recovery. This momentum will sustain RETAIL_REC gains over the next one to two weeks as office workers resume shopping routines.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES improves by more than 2 percentage points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved 3.0 percentage points from t-1w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 7 days does not exceed the prior 7-day mean, or WORKPLACES declines in week t+1.

mechanism_narrative: Stable GROCERY_PHARM (7.3–7.4%) signals essential-goods demand is met without retail substitution. Combined with declining PARKS, consumers have no outdoor leisure alternative and will redirect spending to indoor retail venues, driving RETAIL_REC upward over the next four weeks if GROCERY_PHARM remains stable.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM remains between 6% and 8% AND PARKS remains below -10%
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not exceed the prior 28-day mean, or GROCERY_PHARM falls below 5% or PARKS rises above -5%.
